text:
Salt Lake City reports 6 scams for week ending June 27, 2026
K. E. Gamble
For the week ending June 27, 2026, Salt Lake City had six scam reports, according to Better Business Bureau.
That was down from eight reports in the previous week.
Five of the reports listed losses totaling $1,409.54. Online purchase scams were the most common, accounting for three reports.
The largest reported loss for the week was $1,000 in an online purchase scam. The report stated: "Victor Zane charged me $500 to upgrade my online store. Then he charged me another $500 to b uild a funnel to get customers to my store. I sent gift card that he said was empty, so I sent anoter $500 and got in touch wit Eneba said it had money on it. The store had problems and he wanted $1500 to fix it. I shut it down.I told him to do funnel on another store. He wanted another $300. I asked him for my money back. He said no. It was for service fees. tHERE WERE SMALLER PAYMENTS MADE TO MAKE UP DIFFEERENCE."
BBB Scam Tracker lets consumers search reported scams and post their own experiences to help others spot similar schemes. The BBB says it reviews each report before publication and does not publicly display the reporter's name or personal contact information.
Fraud reports nationwide have continued to show large financial losses. The Federal Trade Commission said consumers reported losing more than $12.5 billion to fraud in 2024, a 25% increase from the previous year.
